Urbie Green has made a career with his trombone in big bands, combos and in the recording studio. Born in Mobile, Alabama in 1926, his first major gig came in the Gene Krupa Orchestra, moving to Woody Herman’s “Third Herd” in 1951. Urbie has worked with Buck Clayton and Benny Goodman and appeared in the film of Goodman’s life. His other big band work includes a short stint with Count Basie and a role of leader with the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra. Urbie can be heard on records with Herbie Mann, Toots Theilmans, Joe Newman and under his own leadership. He currently appears at festivals and jazz parties, often with his son Jesse on piano.
Urbie was interviewed aboard a jazz cruise in the Caribbean on May 29, 1995 by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods.

We are here on behalf of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe, this is Michael Woods, and today we have one of the best known trombone players in jazz — Mr. Urbie Green is with us to talk about his experiences in jazz. Welcome.
Nice to be here, thank you.

It’s a nice setting, we’re on the Royal Caribbean, and Urbie will be playing a set tonight. And we’d like to start off, we’ve had some really interesting talk about how people got started in the music business. Some players happened to fall into circumstances that changed their whole lives; some people kind of had to work for years and years before they found their niche. I wonder if you’d like to talk about that.
